title: Count your known cloud sessions as work on an issue, and stop counting them once deleted
prompt:
The Issues view says who works on an issue (filters, the "taken" chip, the warning before starting a duplicate) from this Mac's sessions and the account's work claims. Account claims arrive late or not at all, so an issue someone has just started in a cloud workspace looks free. The window already holds evidence of those cloud sessions: the cloud dashboard rows, issue pipelines and the starts it made itself. Turn that evidence into issue workers, merge them with arriving claims without counting the same author twice, and make sure a deleted author never comes back because some unrelated cache refreshed. The deletion and timing rules only make sense once the projection and the merge exist.

Work in src/lib/issueWork.ts and wire the result into useIssueWork and the Issues view.

Interface used by other code and tests:
- `interface StartedCloudWork { key; projectPath; issue: IssueRef; at }`.
- `interface CloudWorkInput { projectPath; windowStartedAt; catalog: CloudCatalogState; organizations: readonly string[]; sessions: readonly CloudDashboardSession[]; pipelines: readonly IssuePipeline[]; reviewers: ReadonlySet<string>; started: readonly StartedCloudWork[]; observed?: ReadonlySet<string>; liveSessions(orgId, workspaceId): RuntimeSession[] | null; readerId(orgId, workspaceId): string | null }`. It only reads what the window holds and never connects or writes.
- `cloudWorkers(input, now = Date.now()): Map<string, IssueWorker[]>`, keyed by `workKeyOf(issue)`.
- `IssueWorker` gains `cloudSession?: { key: string; tabId?: string }` (the author's cloud session key and, from a pipeline, the author tab) and `legacyCloudClaimId?: string`. A cloud worker has `place: "cloud"`, `you: true`, `sessionId: null` and `claimSessionId` set to its key.
- `workersByIssue(issues, sessions, remote, now, cloud = new Map())` merges cloud workers with remote claims. A claim for the same session, whether keyed by the full `cloud:org:ws:session` key or by the older organisation-less `cloud:ws:session`, is one worker. That worker keeps cloud navigation and takes live, newer evidence from either side. An offline claim cannot erase live window evidence, and the merge does not change the cloud projection it was given.
- `unavailableText(answer, hasCloud = false)`: when claims are unavailable and cloud work is known, the text mentions "this Mac and your known cloud sessions".

Rules for `cloudWorkers`:
- Only your own authors count. The workspace's `createdBy` must equal `readerId(...)`, except for starts this window made. Reviewers (the input set and pipeline reviewers) never count, and neither do organisations missing from `organizations`, or archived, destroyed or deleted workspaces.
- Organisation, workspace, provider and repository identities stay separate. `projectPath` must match. Equal session ids in two organisations stay distinct. `legacyCloudClaimId` (`cloud:<ws>:<session>`) is set only when exactly one known session has that alias.
- The session list is `liveSessions()` when it is not null, otherwise the catalog's cached list. A session that is archived, or absent from a list after this window observed the author (`observed`), is gone. Later pipeline refreshes (their `place.readAt` advancing) do not bring it back; only the session reappearing does.
- A new author may come before its index entry. It counts while settling: not observed yet, started at or after `windowStartedAt` (by its own start time, either the recorded start's `at` or the pipeline's `created`, never a cache read time), and within twice POLL_MS of that start. After that, absence wins. Pipeline state saved by a previous launch (started before `windowStartedAt`) is not live.
- A successful start counts at once, before the dashboard and pipelines publish it, and stops counting once the session is archived or observed as deleted.
- Saved or cached tab states are not live. A row counts as working or waiting only with runtime evidence: connected, a tab not from the cache, or a recent report. Otherwise the worker is idle.
notes:
Source: PR #616, four commits.
Chain: 54ba18e6 introduces cloudWorkers()/CloudWorkInput in src/lib/issueWork.ts and the merge in workersByIssue, and creates issueWork.cloud.test.ts. abffb7fc changes how those same functions merge a stale window projection with a live claim and how an authoritative removal outlives pipeline-cache refreshes. 2af57a4c changes the settling bound inside cloudWorkers() from pipeline read time to the actual start. 49390bf9 updates the WebKit scenario for the issue-work layout (scripts/webkit/issue-work.mjs) so that it signs in, which the claim hiding needs.
Each later commit edits code the first one introduced, in the same file.
Replaying only the PR's own commits onto startCommit passes the check, so it does not depend on what main merged into the branch.
The check is the PR's issueWork.cloud.test.ts. The IssueWork/IssuesView UI tests are left out.
